title: ר' שמואל בר נחמני

paragraphs:
R' Shmuel bar Nahmani; sometimes bar Nahman. It is all one person. So too it appears in Rashbam, Bava Batra 123a: R' Helbo said to R' Shmuel bar Nahmani, “Your teacher R' Yonatan ….” Rashbam explains that in several places R' Shmuel bar Nahman says in R' Yonatan's name. End of quotation. In Shabbat 116, beginning of side a, and Pesahim 24a: R' Yonatan was R' Shmuel bar Nahmani's teacher. Yuhasin forgot to mention him, though he is mentioned very often in the Talmud. He used to go down לעיבורא [Ibbura; place or intercalation-related activity unresolved] and lodge with R' Yaakov Gerusa. R' Ze'ira would hide to hear how he recited the Shema. He would recite it and repeat it until he sank into sleep; see Ir Binyamin, which gives two explanations of this. Jerusalem Berakhot, first chapter. He refused to release from excommunication a scholar whom Rav Yehudah had excommunicated. R' Zeira said, “What is this—that the old man has not been in the study hall for several years …?” R' Ammi did not release him; see his entry. In Sifrei, Beha'alotekha, the passage “They shall blow on them,” and Rosh Hashanah 34a: it was taught … R' Yishmael son of R' Yohanan says … R' Shmuel bar Nahmani says …. Thus it appears that he was early. “R' Shimon bar Nahmani said, and R' Hanina bar Hama said”: Eikhah Rabbah, at “He has violently stripped his booth like a garden.” It seems to me a scribal error and should read R' Shmuel bar Nahmani. He went up from Babylonia to ask three things, and found Yonatan of Kevurah. He asked him, “What does ‘Open settlements ceased’ mean?”: Midrash Shoher Tov, no. 3; Yalkut Shoftim, chapter 5, remez 49.

Sefer Gilgulei Neshamot writes concerning Ta'anit, first chapter, 8b: in his days there were famine and pestilence. He is Avishai ben Tzeruyah, concerning whom the Holy One, blessed be He, said, “Take the greatest among them as atonement,” for there was famine. Here too he annulled the decree. “His pupil, of R' Abba”; and Abba of Sidon; and a pupil of R' Immi, in R' Shmuel bar Nahman's name. In R' Avdimi of Haifa's name. R' Avahu reports in R' Shmuel bar Nahman's name: Jerusalem Ta'anit, end of chapter 3. R' Aha reports in his name; R' Ahai in his name; R' Ahi in his name; R' Ayvu in his name: Eikhah Rabbah at “The Lord has rejected his altar.” In R' Elyo'enai's name. R' Illa reports in his name; R' Alexandri in his name; R' Berekhiah in his name; R' Berekhiah bar Hama the priest in his name. Rav Huna bar Avin the priest reports in his name. R' Hillel was his son. R' Ze'ira reports in his name: Jerusalem Ta'anit, end of chapter 3. R' Haggai reports in his name; R' Hiyya Kara in his name. R' Hinena. R' Helbo asked him, and said to him, “Because you are a master of aggadah”: Eikhah Rabbah, at “You covered yourself with a cloud.” In R' Yehudah bar Zevida's name. R' Yehudah ben Lekorah reports in his name. R' Yehudah the Nasi said to him, “Because you are a master of aggadah”: Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 12, and Jerusalem Ein Doreshin, end of halakhah 1. One of the rabbis spoke before him in R' Yehoshua ben Levi's name: Pesahim 23b.

He said in R' Yohanan's name: Berakhot 9, end of side b; Shabbat 63b, 75a, 85a. There, 150a, “bar Nehemyah said in R' Yohanan's name” should read Nahmami; so too in Ein Yaakov. Eruvin 100b; Pesahim 49b; Sanhedrin 22b. R' Yohanan's mother spoke to him; see his entry. R' Yohanan of Tzipporin reports in his name. He said in R' Yonatan's name: Berakhot 6b, several matters; there, 7a and 23a, two matters; there, 32a, 35a, 55a–b; Shabbat 56b, several matters; there, 58b, 88b, 89b; Yoma 53a, 72b, 75a, 86b; Sukkah 52b; Megillah 10b; Rosh Hashanah 34a; Yevamot 16b, 105a, 156b; Ketubbot 5, 9 end of side a, “17 het”; Nedarim 22a, 57b; Sotah 11b, 15a; Bava Kamma 60a, 80 end of side b, 85, 92a; Bava Batra 15b; Sanhedrin 3, 14, 20, 29a, 90 end of side a, 93a, 97b, 108b, 110; Avodah Zarah 5a, 18 end of side b; Hullin 10b; Menahot 29a, 99b; Arakhin 11a; and Jerusalem Keitzad Mevarekhin. In Yalkut Tehillim, chapter 19, “in R' Natan's name” is a scribal error and should read Yonatan. He asked Yonatan of Kevurah; see his entry. He said in R' Yonatan ben Elazar's name: Yelammedenu, Behukkotai.

He disagrees with R' Yaakov bar Idi. R' Yitzhak ben Pazi was in his time. R' Yitzhak was his brother; Levi his son. And R' Mattanah: Jerusalem Berakhot, first chapter. R' Nahman was his son. R' Simon reports in his name: Jerusalem Megillah, chapter 1. And R' Simon bar Zavdi. Yuhasin writes that R' Kasda was in his time; I did not find this. רבב״ח [provisionally Rabbah bar bar Hana] was in his time. “Rabbi said: ‘In place of his glory …’”: Shabbat 113, end of side b; but in Ein Yaakov and the new Talmud editions the word Rabbi is absent. “He went down to bathe and saw Rabbi”: Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 63. R' Shimon Kamtarya reports in his name. R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak said to him, “You are a master of aggadah.” R' Tahlifa, R' Aha's father-in-law, reports in his name.
